Issues.Title: Fix issue 15350: Multiple KioskModeManager components using the same ToggleFullScreenKeys prevent exiting full-screen mode
Issues.Body: Fixes #15350 ## Root Cause Each KioskModeManager registered as an IMessageFilter independently processed the same keyboard shortcut. Because the filter did not report the shortcut as handled, multiple managers could toggle full-screen in sequence—for example, one manager entered full-screen and another immediately exited it. ## Proposed changes Make keyboard activity processing report whether it handled the message. When a manager handles its configured full-screen toggle shortcut or Escape-to-exit action, return true from ProcessMessage so subsequent message filters do not process the same key. Add regression coverage for multiple managers using the same shortcut. ## Customer Impact Make keyboard activity processing report whether it handled the message. Issues.Title: Add tests for Form DPI change handling
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- Existing DPI tests only poke individual controls with `WM_DPICHANGED_BEFOREPARENT`/`AFTERPARENT`; nothing drove a top-level `Form` through `WM_DPICHANGED`. Added `FormTests.DpiChanged.cs` to cover that.
- Tests (run in a PerMonitorV2 child process via `RemoteExecutor`, like the existing nested-container DPI test):
  - `DpiChanged` reports the old/new DPI and suggested rectangle, the form moves to that rectangle, and `DeviceDpi` updates on the form and its nested children. Child before/after-parent events use plain `EventArgs` and see the new DPI.
  - Moving to a higher DPI and back three times, using `WM_GETDPISCALEDSIZE`, returns the original form size and keeps child bounds within 1px (no drift).
  - A handler setting `Cancel` leaves bounds untouched but still records the new DPI.
  - A message carrying the current DPI raises no event and changes nothing.
- No product code changes.

## Customer Impact

- None, test-only.

## Regression?

- No

## Risk

- Minimal, test-only.

Issues.Title: Add handle recreation tests for Control
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- Existing `RecreateHandle` tests only checked that the handle value changed. This adds tests in `ControlTests.HandleRecreation.cs` for the behavior around recreation.
- `RecreatingHandle` is true while `HandleDestroyed` and `HandleCreated` run, with the old window still valid in the first and the new one valid in the second. Events fire once each and name, text, bounds and parent are kept.
- Children and grandchildren keep valid windows and are re-parented to the new parent window.
- `RecreateHandle` is a no-op without a handle or after dispose. When `CreateHandle` throws during recreation, the control ends up without a handle and `RecreatingHandle` is cleared.
- Style-dependent setters preserve state: `TextBox.Multiline` (text and selection), `ListBox.MultiColumn` (items and selection), `ListView.Scrollable` (items, checked state, selection).
- A main `Form` whose handle is recreated via `ShowInTaskbar` doesn't make its `ApplicationContext` raise `ThreadExit`; disposing it does.

No product code changes.

## Customer Impact

- None; test-only change.

## Regression?

- No

## Risk

- Minimal; tests only.

Issues.Title: Toolbox is empty and Panel is missing from Document Outline (.NET 10, out-of-process designer)
Issues.Body: ### Environment Version 18.12.0 ### .NET version .NET 10 ### Did this work in a previous version of Visual Studio and/or previous .NET release? _No response_ ### Issue description In a .NET 10.0 WinForms project, a standard System.Windows.Forms.Panel that is dock-enabled through a third-party extender component cannot be used as a normal container in the out-of-process designer: 1. When the Panel is selected on the design surface, the Toolbox shows no controls (it is empty or greyed out). 2. Controls cannot be dragged from the Toolbox into the Panel. 3. The Panel is not shown in the Document Outline window. 4. The Panel is not visible on the design surface, although the application renders it correctly at runtime. Expected: A Panel that is dock-enabled by an extender provider should remain a selectable container. It should show in Document Outline, the Toolbox should be enabled when it is selected, and drops should be accepted. Actual: The Panel behaves as if it were not a container in the designer. I would like to know whether this is expected for extender providers in the out-of-process designer, and what the designer expects from such a component (for example a custom ControlDesigner or a required designer-host service). I could not find guidance in the documentation. Sample project: [Core.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35029435/Core.zip) Video reference: ### Steps to reproduce Open the sample project Drag and drop the CustomDockingManager component onto the form. Drag and drop the Customdockpanel control onto the CustomDockingManager. With designer open, Focus the customdockpanel and see the ToolBox no items are available to drag and drop. Issues.Title: Fix issue 15351: The exception appeared when switch the value form Form1 to UserControl item for the ContainerControl  property

Fixes #15351 

## Root Cause

KioskModeManager.ContainerControl is an expandable property.
In PropertyGrid, when this property is changed from Form to UserControl while it is not expanded, stale child-property cache/state can remain. Expanding it afterward may then access outdated child entries and trigger an exception.
If the property is expanded first, PropertyGrid follows a child-recreation path, which is why the issue is less likely to reproduce.

Issues.Title: Add native handle lifetime tests for Control
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- The existing create/destroy/dispose tests for `Control` mostly assert managed state (`IsHandleCreated`, `Created`, event counts). They never check the native window itself.
- Add `ControlTests.HandleLifetime.cs`, which checks the real HWND:
  - Reading `Handle` creates one valid window owned by the current thread and process, raises `HandleCreated` once, and maps back via `Control.FromHandle`.
  - `DestroyHandle` raises `HandleDestroyed` while the window still exists, then the window is gone and detached. A new handle is a different, valid window.
  - `Dispose` with a handle raises `HandleDestroyed` once and destroys the window. `Handle` and `CreateHandle` then throw `ObjectDisposedException`, and a second `Dispose` does nothing.
  - Repeated create/destroy cycles give a new valid window each time, with matching event counts. Name, Text, Tag, BackColor, Enabled, Bounds, Parent and children are preserved.
  - Destroying or disposing a parent destroys child windows. `CreateControl` on the parent recreates the child window.
- No product code changes.

## Customer Impact

- None. Test-only change.

## Regression?

- No

## Risk

- Minimal. Tests only.

Issues.Title: Fix FlatAppearance color overrides for non-flat buttons in Net11 and dark mode
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15439

## Root cause

Dark-mode and Net11 button renderers applied `FlatAppearance` settings to non-Flat styles. This included not only border and interaction colors, but also `BorderSize`, which could affect Popup button rendering and preferred size. Modern CheckBox and RadioButton glyph renderers also applied `BorderColor` outside Flat style.

## Proposed changes

- Honor `FlatAppearance` settings only when `FlatStyle` is `Flat`.
- Ignore `BorderSize` as well as border, checked, hover, and pressed colors for non-Flat styles, including Popup sizing and animated rendering.
- Apply the same Flat-style restriction to modern CheckBox and RadioButton glyph border colors.
- Keep the configured values intact so they take effect again if the control is switched to Flat style.
- Add regression coverage for Net11, Classic dark mode, Popup preferred size, and modern glyph controls.

Issues.Body: Fixes #15427 ## Root Cause ButtonBaseAdapter.DrawImageCore used graphics.DrawImageUnscaled(image, imageBounds.Location) when DotNetOneButtonCompat == false and the control was enabled. In the .NET 11 modern/owner-drawn button rendering path, this call can produce inconsistent rendering for PNG images (especially with DPI metadata), causing images to appear magnified or partially visible. ## Proposed changes - Remove the DrawImageUnscaled branch and use a single enabled-path draw call: graphics.DrawImage(image, imageBounds.X, imageBounds.Y, image.Width, image.Height). - Keep the existing clipping behavior: intersect with imageBounds only when layout squeezes the image, so non-squeezed images keep edge pixels. - Add ButtonBaseAdapterTests covering combinations of graphics DPI, image DPI, ClipImagesToClient on/off, and squeezed/non-squeezed layout to verify pixel size and clipping behavior. ## Customer Impact - Fixes the .NET 11 regression where button foreground PNG images could render as magnified or missing/partially clipped. - Restores behavior closer to .NET 10 across DPI and image-resolution combinations. - Change scope is limited to button foreground image rendering logic, with targeted regression coverage and passing related tests. ## Regression? - Yes - #14809 ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Manual - Automation test ## Test environment(s) - 12.0.0-alpha.1.26565.104 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15441)

Issues.Title: Fix button background artifacts after parent color changes
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15434

## Root cause

Buttons with an explicit `BackColor` were not invalidated when their parent's background color changed. Their existing pixels could retain the old parent color.

## Proposed changes

- Invalidate owner-drawn `ButtonBase` controls with an explicit background color when their parent's background changes in Net11 visual styles mode.
- Preserve existing ambient-color and native-rendering behavior.
- Add regression tests and update the unshipped API list.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

-  Buttons with a custom background color repaint when their parent’s background color changes, preventing stale rectangular artifacts without requiring mouse interaction.

## Regression? 

-  No

## Risk

- Low: affected modern owner-drawn controls receive an additional invalidation when the parent background color changes.

## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before
Changing a form's background color could leave rectangular artifacts around buttons until they were repainted, for example on hover.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c49620cc-566c-419f-baed-3947712eb471


### After
Affected buttons are invalidated when the parent color changes, allowing them to repaint with the new background.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25ddb33f-ddb6-47bd-9960-c309b72d1da5

-  Unit tests and manual tests

Issues.Title: Button retains previous Form background color when Form.BackColor changes in VisualStylesMode.NET11
Issues.Body: ### .NET version .NET 12 SDK build: 12.0.100-alpha.1.26565.104 ### Did it work in .NET Framework? Not tested/verified ### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+? New APIs in .NET 11 introduced ### Issue description When using VisualStylesMode.NET11, changing the Form's BackColor after setting a custom BackColor on Button controls causes rendering artifacts around the buttons. Some areas surrounding the buttons retain the previous Form background color instead of updating to the new color. The issue occurs in both the WinForms Designer and at runtime. Manually triggering a refresh restores the correct appearance. Designer time: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22270eaa-3801-4039-b18a-d9e8144546c9 Runtime: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45d79584-8fe4-44cc-bd17-d334b32c0ce4 The issue does not reproduce when the buttons use their default BackColor. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a WinForms application targeting .NET 11. 2. Set VisualStylesMode to NET11. 3. Add several Button controls to the Form. 4. Set their FlatStyle properties to Standard, Flat, Popup, and System, respectively. 5. Set the Form's BackColor to a custom color. 6. Set the buttons' BackColor to a different custom color. 7. Change the Form's BackColor to another color in an event For example: the Form's BackColor can be changed through a Button click event: ``` private void button9_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { this.BackColor = Color.Purple; } ``` 8. Observe the areas surrounding the buttons. [WinFormsApp38.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34903117/WinFormsApp38.zip)

Issues.Title: Add ComboBox item editing and DPI autocomplete handle creation tests
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

ComboBox had little coverage for editing items and text against the native list, and the existing DPI-driven handle creation test only covered one parent type, one autocomplete source and one scale direction.

- Items: add/insert/remove/clear, `Sorted`, items added before the handle, `AddRange` with a null element, `BeginUpdate`/`EndUpdate`, and clearing a `DataSource` are all checked against the native list (`CB_GETCOUNT`/`CB_GETLBTEXT`) for each `DropDownStyle`.
- Selection and text: selection after remove/clear, `Text` per `DropDownStyle` (with and without a handle, case differences, non-matching text), and a single `SelectedIndexChanged`/`TextChanged` when selecting an item.
- DPI handle creation: nested parent, scaling up and down, list-items and custom autocomplete sources, all autocomplete modes, a `FontChanged` handler that changes the font again, and a later handle recreate. Each checks that the handle is created once, never recursively, and autocomplete stays initialized.

No product-code changes. A real monitor DPI change can't be automated, so the DPI tests simulate a mismatch the same way the existing test does.

## Validation

- `.\build.cmd -verbosity minimal`: succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `System.Windows.Forms.Tests.exe --filter-class System.Windows.Forms.Tests.ComboBoxTests`: 976 passed, 0 failed, run five times in a row, non-elevated.
